transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Vikram Desai?

Customer: Haan, yes, this is Vikram. Who is calling, sir?

Agent: Hi Vikram, this is Rohit from Finserve Collections. I'm calling about your personal loan account, the one ending in 5649. You have a few minutes, na?

Customer: <interruption> Uh, yeah, okay. But I'm getting too many calls, yaar. Every day, every day only calling.

Agent: I understand, Vikram. This will be quick. So, your account is currently overdue by 52 days now. The EMI of 13,800 rupees was due on the 18th of last month, and we haven't received anything yet. Can you help me understand what's happening with the payment?

Customer: Hmm, yes, I know about this. See, the thing is... <interruption> my company, the IT firm where I was working as a senior developer, na... they suddenly shut down operations. Just like that, two months back. No notice, nothing. One day they called everyone and said the office is closing permanently.

Agent: Oh, I see. That must be very difficult, Vikram. When exactly did this happen?

Customer: It was... maybe 58, 60 days back now. I was there for almost nine years, doing good work also. But they gave us only two weeks' salary and that's it. No severance, no nothing. So right now, my friend, I have zero income coming in.

Agent: Okay, okay. Have you found any other work since then?

Customer: No, yaar, nothing yet. I've been applying here and there, submitting CVs to so many companies, but dekho, the market is very slow right now. I have my wife and one daughter, she's in school. My father also stays with us now. So you can imagine, na, the pressure is there.

Agent: Yes, I can understand. Before this job loss, you were paying your EMIs on time, correct?

Customer: <interruption> Haan, bilkul. Never missed one payment before this. But now, uh, my wife she does some work from home, tutoring and all, she's making maybe 7,500 rupees per month, that's it. How can I pay 13,800 when only 7,500 is coming in? And rent is 14,000, school fees 4,500, food and everything... it's not possible, sir.

Agent: I hear you. So the job loss is the main reason you haven't been able to pay the EMI?

Customer: Yes, yes, exactly. It's not that I don't want to pay, na. I have responsibility. But there is no income. What can I do? I've been going to interviews, uh, submitting applications, but nothing concrete yet. Maybe next month or two months, I'm hoping, but I cannot say for sure.

Agent: Understood, Vikram. And your wife's income of 7,500 — is that regular every month?

Customer: Hmm, sometimes it's 7,500, sometimes maybe 8,000 if she gets more students. But mostly around that only. And I have, uh, some savings also, but that is finishing very quickly now. Maybe one and a half months left, then finished.

Agent: I see. So there's a significant gap every month. What are your total household expenses roughly?

Customer: <interruption> Rent 14,000, school fees 4,500, food maybe 7,000, utilities and phone 1,500, medicines and healthcare another 1,500 for my father... so around 28,500 to 29,000 per month. And my wife earning only 7,500, na.

Agent: That's a shortfall of about 21,000 rupees every month. Have you looked into any government assistance or unemployment benefits?

Customer: No, no, I didn't know about that. Is there something like that available? I should check, maybe.

Agent: Yes, there are some schemes, you can look into separately. For now, Vikram, based on what you're telling me, this looks like a genuine hardship case due to job loss and income disruption. I need to escalate this to our hardship assessment team. They will contact you within two to three business days with restructuring options.

Customer: Okay, so what options are there? Can I get some relief or something?

Agent: Yes, possible options could be extending your loan tenure to reduce the monthly EMI, or we might offer a temporary payment moratorium for a few months. But nothing is guaranteed until the formal assessment is done, understand?

Customer: Okay, I understand, sir. So I don't need to pay the full 13,800 right now?

Agent: Not immediately, no. But Vikram, it's important you keep looking for employment actively, and if anything changes, please call us right away. Can I update your contact number in our records?

Customer: The number you called me on is correct, yaar.

Agent: Perfect. I'm noting this as a job loss hardship case. Our team will contact you very soon. In the meantime, keep applying for jobs and let us know immediately if your situation improves. Okay?

Customer: Yes, thank you. I appreciate this, sir. Thank you for understanding.

Agent: You're welcome, Vikram. We'll be in touch shortly. Have a good day.

Customer: Thank you, sir. Bye.

Customer: Haan, yes, this is Rajesh. Who is calling?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Priya from Allied Finance Collections. I'm calling regarding your loan account ending in 4521. You have an outstanding amount of 47,380 rupees due since the 15th of last month. Can we discuss your payment plan today?

Customer: Look, I don't know what's happening, but this is the third time someone is calling me today. Third time! In the morning, then afternoon, and now evening. It's almost 8 PM. I was having dinner with my family, and you people keep calling. This is too much.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. I apologize for any inconvenience. We do need to collect the outstanding amount. Can I just confirm your current address so we can update our records?

Customer: No, no, no. Don't update anything. I want to know — why are you calling me so many times? This is harassment, yaar. I received calls at 7:45 AM also, which is before your official hours. I checked the time. And yesterday, someone from your company called my office and asked my manager if I was present. My manager! They told my manager about my loan. How is that even allowed?

Agent: I apologize for that, Rajesh. That must have been frustrating. But regarding the outstanding amount—

Customer: <interruption> No, listen. This is not acceptable. I am going to file a complaint with the RBI. I am serious. You people are violating my privacy. Calling my office, calling me every hour, calling after 7 PM. This is not how you should treat customers. I have already taken screenshots of all the calls and the times. I'm also thinking of posting this on social media, on Twitter, and telling everyone about how Allied Finance harasses its customers.

Agent: Rajesh, I understand you're upset. Let me escalate this to my supervisor. But first, can we just—

Customer: No supervisor. I don't want to talk to anyone else right now. What I want is for the calling to stop. And I want a written apology from your company about contacting my office. Until you fix this, I don't want to hear from Allied Finance again. Not by phone, not by SMS, nothing. This is my formal request. Do not contact me anymore without a letter explaining the breach of privacy.

Agent: I hear you, Rajesh. I will escalate this to our compliance team immediately. Your request will be logged as a do-not-contact, and I will mark this account for a review. Can I at least note down your preferred contact method going forward?

Customer: Email. Only email. And make sure this complaint reaches your senior management. I am documenting everything. If I don't get a proper response within 7 days, I will escalate to the consumer forum as well. This is not just about the money anymore. This is about how you treat people.

Agent: Understood, Rajesh. I have logged your complaint and your do-not-contact request. Your email is rajesh.kumar.1987@email.com, correct?

Customer: Yes, that's correct. And I want confirmation that you've escalated this to compliance. Can you give me a reference number?

Agent: Your complaint reference number is CC-2024-114789. This will be escalated to our compliance and grievance team within the next 24 hours. They will contact you via email with a formal response. I sincerely apologize for the experience you've had.

Customer: Fine. But remember — no more calls. Only email. And get this sorted.

Agent: Noted, Rajesh. Thank you for your patience. Have a good evening.

Agent: Hello, this is Rajesh from Creditsure Collections. May I please speak with Mr. Anand Kapoor?

Customer: Yes, this is he speaking. But listen, I have already received a summons from the court. My lawyer is handling this matter now, so I am not sure why you are calling me.

Agent: I understand, Mr. Kapoor. I can see here that we have been trying to reach you regarding your outstanding loan balance of 4,87,000 rupees. Your account has been delinquent for over 180 days now. Can you help me understand the situation?

Customer: Look, I got the legal notice two weeks back. The court has issued summons and my lawyer told me not to speak directly to you people. He said everything should go through him now. But since you are on the line, let me be clear — I want to settle this before it goes further into the courts. I cannot afford the legal fees on top of everything else.

Agent: I appreciate you sharing that, Mr. Kapoor. This is helpful information. So you are open to resolving this matter, but your legal representation is in place. Can you tell me — what settlement amount would you be willing to work towards?

Customer: See, the thing is, I lost my job around eight months ago. My wife's salary alone is not enough to cover all the EMIs I have. I have been trying to find work, but the market is bad right now. I got this summons and now I am panicking. The original loan amount was around 5 lakhs, and I have paid maybe 40,000 rupees so far. But the outstanding amount you are showing includes a lot of interest and penalty charges that I think are not correct.

Agent: I understand your hardship, Mr. Kapoor. Regarding the charges, I can pull up your statement and we can review it together. But first — you mentioned your lawyer is handling this. Does your lawyer have authority to negotiate a settlement on your behalf, or do you need to speak with him before we discuss any figures?

Customer: <interruption> No, no, I... I can at least explore what is possible. My lawyer said I should try to settle before it becomes a full court case. So what are you offering? Can you reduce the amount because of the penalties? I am willing to pay, but not the full 4,87,000.

Agent: That is a fair question. Based on your situation — job loss, ongoing financial difficulty — I can present a settlement proposal to our senior team. However, any settlement will require your legal representative's concurrence since court proceedings are active. What would be a realistic amount you could manage? And when could you arrange that payment?

Customer: If I can get my severance package next month — it should come through in about four to five weeks — I could pay maybe 2,50,000 rupees as a one-time settlement. That is almost half. But my lawyer needs to approve this, and I need this in writing from your side before I commit to anything. I am not going to promise something and then get trapped.

Agent: That is very reasonable, Mr. Kapoor. A settlement of 2,50,000 rupees contingent on your severance arrival is something I can escalate to our legal team immediately. They will prepare a formal settlement sanction letter for your review and your lawyer's review. In the meantime, I need to log this as a settlement response to active legal proceedings. Can you confirm your current contact number is still 98765-43210?

Customer: Yes, that is correct. But please make sure you send the settlement letter to my lawyer as well. His name is Advocate Deepak Sharma, and his office email is deepak.sharma.advocate@email.com. Do not send anything to me directly without copying him. This is important.

Agent: Absolutely, Mr. Kapoor. I have noted that all settlement communications must go through Advocate Deepak Sharma. I will ensure the legal team coordinates directly with him. They will prepare the sanction letter and send it to both you and your lawyer for review. Once you receive the severance, you can then proceed with the settlement payment. This call will be escalated to our legal department for next steps. Thank you for your cooperation despite the difficult circumstances.

Customer: Okay, thank you. I appreciate this. Just... please follow up with my lawyer. Do not keep calling me on this number. Everything should go through him now.

Agent: Understood, Mr. Kapoor. No further calls will be made to your personal number. All future communication will be routed through Advocate Deepak Sharma. We will be in touch via him. Thank you, and I hope your situation improves.

Customer: Thank you. Goodbye.

Agent: Goodbye, Mr. Kapoor.

Agent: Hello, is this Rajesh Kumar speaking?

Agent: I see. Can you tell me more about that? When exactly did you settle the account, Rajesh?

Customer: It was... I think around March. Yes, March this year. I paid the final amount and the bank sent me a closure letter. No Objection Certificate. So I don't understand why your system is still showing this as active. This is really frustrating, yaar. I've already cleared everything.

Agent: Okay, I understand your frustration. Let me just verify the details here. So you're saying you made a full repayment and received an NOC from us in March?

Customer: Not from you people, no. From the previous lender. The account was with another bank before, and I settled with them. They gave me the NOC. Agent: Yes, that's the outstanding amount on the file. So just to clarify — you had the loan with another lender first, and you settled that account?

Customer: Exactly. I paid off the entire loan. They sent me the NOC. I have it somewhere, I can find it. Why would I pay again? The loan is closed. There's nothing outstanding from my side.

Agent: I appreciate you explaining this, Rajesh. It sounds like there may be some confusion between accounts. Can you tell me which bank the original loan was with? And do you remember the loan account number from that bank?

Customer: It was... I think it was with Metro Bank. The account number I don't recall exactly, but it was definitely with them. And then somehow FinServe is showing this same loan as active, which doesn't make sense. Either you've pulled in old data, or the account was never properly closed on your system after the settlement.

Agent: I see. So you're saying you may have taken a new loan with us after settling the Metro Bank account? Or is this the same loan that was transferred?

Customer: No, no, I don't think so. I only took one personal loan. After I settled it with Metro Bank and got the NOC, that should have been the end. I didn't take another loan with you people. This is <interruption> this is the same loan, but it should be closed. Closed and done.

Agent: Okay, Rajesh. I'm going to need to verify this against our records. It's possible the account was transferred from Metro Bank to our portfolio, and the closure may not have been properly reflected in our system. I'll need to check with my supervisor and pull up the settlement documentation.

Customer: Yes, please do that. Because I'm not paying anything on an account that I've already settled. Once you verify that the loan is indeed closed with the NOC, we can be done with this, and you can stop calling me.

Agent: Understood. I'll escalate this to my supervisor today and we'll check the settlement records and the NOC documentation. Can I call you back tomorrow afternoon with an update? Would 3 PM work?

Customer: Yes, 3 PM is fine. But please, make sure you check properly. I don't want to keep getting these calls if the account is already closed.

Customer: <interruption> Haan haan, but actually... look, I need to tell you something. Rajesh is not... Rajesh passed away. He passed away three months back. I am his brother, Vikram. I am speaking on his behalf.

Agent: Oh, I am very sorry to hear that. My condolences to the family. So Vikram ji, you are the... are you the next of kin?

Customer: Yes, yes, I am the elder brother. After he died, I have been trying to sort out his things. The house, the bank, everything. Very difficult situation, sir. Very difficult.

Agent: I understand, Vikram ji. This must be very challenging. Can you tell me — was Rajesh the sole applicant on this loan, or is there a co-applicant or guarantor on the account?

Customer: No, no, he was alone. He took this loan alone in 2021. At that time he was working in Infosys, he was earning well. But then in 2022 he lost his job, and... and then his health became very bad. He had a heart condition. The doctors said he needed surgery. So he did the surgery but... but he could not recover properly. Three months back, he just... he went.

Agent: I see. And Vikram ji, has the account been informed of his passing? Has the bank received any official notification?

Customer: No, no, I haven't done that yet. I have been so busy with the funeral, the cremation, the legal papers for the property. I didn't even think about calling the bank. That is why I am very surprised you called today. Usually you call him on his mobile, not this number. This is the landline at the house.

Agent: Yes, I see. We had dialled the registered number and you picked up. Vikram ji, I have to be honest with you — we cannot continue with normal collection activity on this account now that I know the borrower is no longer alive. This is a very sensitive matter and it needs to be handled properly. 

Customer: Okay, okay, but what does this mean? Will I have to pay this loan? Will it become my responsibility? He did not leave any life insurance. He did not leave any money either. There are medical bills still pending, and the house... I don't know if the house is in his name only or if there are other issues.

Agent: That is a very good question, and I cannot answer that on this call. What I will do now is escalate this account to our bereavement team and to our legal team. They will review the situation and they will determine what the proper course of action is. They may contact you within the next few days, but it will be with sensitivity. They are trained for these situations.

Customer: Okay, okay. Should I also call the bank myself? Should I submit some documents? I have the death certificate, the cremation certificate, everything.

Agent: Yes, Vikram ji, absolutely. You should inform the bank officially with those documents. Send them a copy of the death certificate, the cremation certificate, and any proof that you are the legal heir or next of kin. You can also write a letter to the bank informing them of the death. This will create an official record.

Customer: Alright, alright. And this loan... will it affect my credit? I am also having a personal loan with another bank and I am paying that on time. Will this affect that?

Agent: That is also something the legal and bereavement team will clarify with you. Once they contact you, please be honest and transparent with them about the situation. They will guide you properly. For now, I want you to know that we understand your situation and we are not going to harass you with collection calls while this is being resolved.

Customer: Thank you, sir. That is... that is a relief. I was very worried. I did not know what to do. Thank you for understanding.

Agent: You are welcome, Vikram ji. I will make a note on the account right now. Our team will reach out to you within 48 hours. Please keep the death certificate and other documents ready. And if you have any questions in the meantime, you can also call back on this number and ask for the bereavement team. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

Customer: No, no, I think that is all. Thank you again. I will wait for your team to contact me.

Agent: Thank you, Vikram ji. My sincere condolences once again to you and your family. Take care.

Customer: Arrey, I need to check with my wife first. She handles the accounts, na. Plus, last time you people gave me a settlement offer and then the terms changed when I went to the branch. I don't trust this anymore. <interruption> Why should I agree when the same thing might happen again?

Customer: No, no. I cannot commit without seeing something in writing and without discussing with my wife. And frankly, even one-forty is stretching it. If you can come down to one lakh, maybe I can convince her. Otherwise, I don't see how I can do this.

Customer: Haan, haan, I know, I know. Ma'am, actually I was going to... I mean, I wanted to call you people myself, na. But listen, I had a small shop — garment business in Colaba, Mumbai. Business was going really well, everything was fine until last month when... when the monsoon rains came. The whole basement, the entire basement got flooded, ma'am. Everything — all my inventory, the stock, everything was destroyed. Water damage, stock loss, I'm telling you, everything is gone.

Agent: Oh no, that's very difficult, Rajesh. I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me more about how this flood has affected your business and your ability to pay right now?

Customer: The impact is... it's massive, na. I've lost maybe 15 to 20 lakh rupees worth of garments. The shop building itself needs repairs — the walls are damaged, the electrical wiring is all... it's all damaged. And the worst part, the worst part is the municipal authorities, they have sealed the shop. They sealed it pending inspection and safety clearance, so I cannot operate at all right now.

Agent: So your business is completely shut down because of the municipal seal?

Customer: Exactly, exactly. No revenue coming in. None. Zero. I've been trying to get the insurance claim processed, but it's very slow, na. They are saying two, three months minimum for the claim. Meanwhile, I have no income, nothing. My family is depending on this shop's income, and I have this EMI of 18,500 every month. Plus I have another loan from HDFC Bank — another 12,000 rupees EMI — so together it's about 30,000 every month I need to pay. How can I pay when there's no money coming in?

Agent: I understand. You have multiple EMI obligations and the flood has completely disrupted your income. Have you been able to make any partial payment towards this account, or is it completely blocked right now?

Customer: Nothing, ma'am. I have no money right now. I've been taking small loans from my family members just to eat and pay for some of the repairs. The insurance claim will come, but that's two, three months away. By that time, I don't know what will happen to my account status. I'm not trying to avoid payment, I'm not. I want to pay, but I literally have no income.

Agent: I see. And when do you expect the shop to reopen? Has the municipal inspection been scheduled?

Customer: They said maybe two, three weeks for the inspection, then another week or two for repairs and... and reopening. But honestly, even after reopening, it will take time to rebuild the stock, get back to normal business. I'm looking at maybe two months, minimum, before I can generate proper income again. This is a disaster, ma'am. A complete disaster.

Agent: Rajesh, I want to help you here. This is clearly an external event beyond your control — the flood damage and shop closure are legitimate hardship factors. Have you been able to document this? Do you have photographs of the damage, the municipal seal notice, anything like that?

Customer: Yes, actually I have. I took photos of everything — the water damage, the ruined garments, the municipal notice on my door. I can send these to you if needed.
